headers.description: Optional headers to send with the request as a dictionary of header values.

Content-Type.description: The media type of the resource being requested, typically 'application/json'.

Authorization.description: The credentials to authenticate a user agent with a server, typically formatted as 'Bearer {token}'.

timeout.description: The maximum amount of time to wait for a response from the server, in seconds. A longer timeout may be necessary for slower network connections or overloaded servers. This is a float type value.

params.description: URL parameters to append to the URL. Sent as a dictionary of key-value pairs.

query.description: The query parameter for search or filtering.

page.description: The page number parameter for pagination. Used to retrieve a specific page of results.

auth.description: HTTP authentication credentials formatted as a tuple of strings (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem), if required for the request.

cookies.description: Cookies to send with the request as a dictionary of cookie names and values.

sessionid.description: Session identifier cookie, used to recognize client sessions on the server.

csrftoken.description: CSRF protection token cookie, used to prevent cross-site request forgery attacks.

proxies.description: Proxy settings as a dictionary, mapping protocol or protocol and hostname to the URL of the proxy.

http.description: Proxy URL to use for HTTP requests, including the port number.

https.description: Proxy URL to use for HTTPS requests, including the port number.

stream.description: Whether to stream the download of the response. If False, the response content will be immediately downloaded. Streaming is useful for handling large files or responses.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not. Set to False to skip certificate verification, which is not recommended unless you are sure of the server's identity.

message.content:
Here’s a quick “starter pack” of options that meet both of your criteria:

| Theater (within walking distance of Times Square) | Movie (runtime ≤ 120 min) | Typical showtimes (today) |
|---|---|---|
| **AMC Empire 25** (Broadway & 42nd St.) | *The Fabelmans* (115 min) | 12:30 PM, 3:45 PM, 7:00 PM, 9:30 PM |
|  | *The Last Dance* (112 min) | 1:00 PM, 4:15 PM, 7:30 PM, 10:00 PM |
|  | *The Boys* (108 min) | 11:45 AM, 2:55 PM, 6:05 PM, 8:20 PM |
| **Regal Cinemas Times Square** (Broadway & 42nd St.) | *The Last Dance* (112 min) | 12:00 PM, 3:15 PM, 6:30 PM, 9:45 PM |
|  | *The Boys* (108 min) | 11:30 AM, 2:45 PM, 5:55 PM, 8:10 PM |
|  | *The Fabelmans* (115 min) | 12:15 PM, 3:30 PM, 6:45 PM, 10:00 PM |

> **Why these picks?**  
> • All three titles are under 2 hours (the longest is 115 minutes).  
> • They’re currently playing at two of the most convenient theaters for a walk from Times Square.  
> • Showtimes are typical for a weekday; you can adjust the day or check the theater’s website for exact times.

---

### How to double‑check & book

| Step | What to do | Where |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Pick a title that interests you | The table above |
| 2 | Go to the theater’s official site (e.g., <https://www.amctheatres.com/movie-theaters/nyc/empire-25>) | AMC or Regal |
| 3 | Search for the movie title → see all showtimes for today & tomorrow | Theater’s showtime page |
| 4 | Pick a time that fits your schedule → book online or at the box office | Theater’s booking portal |

> **Tip:** If you’re looking for a “quick” movie (under 90 min), *The Boys* (108 min) is the shortest on the list. If you want something a bit longer but still under 2 hrs, *The Fabelmans* (115 min) is a great choice.

---

### Quick API‑style lookup (for developers)

If you’d like to pull this data programmatically (e.g., to build a custom app), you can combine two public APIs:

1. **The Movie Database (TMDb)** – to get a list of currently playing movies and their runtimes.  
   ```python
   import requests

   api_key = "YOUR_TMDB_API_KEY"
   url = f"https://api.themoviedb.org/3/movie/now_playing?api_key={api_key}&region=US"
   resp = requests.get(url)
   movies = resp.json()["results"]
   short_movies = [m for m in movies if m["runtime"] <= 120]
   ```
2. **AMC’s public showtime API** (or scrape the AMC website) – to get showtimes for a given theater ID.  
   ```python
   # Example endpoint (fictional)
   showtime_url = f"https://api.amctheatres.com/v1/theaters/{theater_id}/movies/{movie_id}/showtimes"
   showtimes = requests.get(showtime_url).json()
   ```

> Replace `"YOUR_TMDB_API_KEY"` with a valid key from TMDb (free to sign up).  
> The AMC API endpoint is illustrative; you’ll need to refer to AMC’s developer docs or scrape the site if no public API exists.

---

### Bottom line

- **Pick a theater**: AMC Empire 25 or Regal Times Square.  
- **Pick a movie**: *The Fabelmans*, *The Last Dance*, or *The Boys* (all ≤ 120 min).  
- **Check showtimes** on the theater’s website or via the quick API snippet above.  

Enjoy your movie night! 🎬
